entities.name: PMID:25423144
observations: In nude mice, serial 4.7-T T1, T2, T2*, and ADC measurements of implanted human rectus-abdominis muscle precursor cells shifted from high early-stage values toward mature skeletal-muscle values during differentiation.
Differentiation was validated by immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and contraction assays; fibroblast, prostate-cancer-cell, and collagen controls were included.

entities.name: PMID:25710336
observations: Contemporaneous commentary interpreted MR relaxation and diffusion measurements as detecting differentiation of implanted human muscle precursor cells into mature skeletal muscle.
The approach was described as label-free and potentially useful for monitoring muscle cell therapy.

entities.name: PMID:20643023
observations: Ferritin-engineered C2C12 myoblasts produced T2 shortening and hypointense grafts after transplantation; MRI-estimated graft size correlated with histology (R²=0.8).
The study supports graft localization and size estimation, not a direct MRI readout of differentiation state.

entities.name: MRI differentiation characterization
observations: Multiparametric relaxometry with diffusion can noninvasively characterize in-vivo maturation of transplanted human muscle precursor-cell tissue when paired with histologic and functional validation.
T1, T2, and T2* changes are not intrinsically specific for differentiation because water content, edema, inflammation, extracellular matrix, iron, necrosis, and injury can also alter relaxation.
